name: Few-shot Example Curator
blurb: few-shot examples balanced by label, deduplicated, ordered and fitted to a token budget
intro: Picks and orders few-shot examples from a pool: labels read from the outputs, near-duplicates found by the Jaccard index of character 5-gram shingles, contradictions (same input, different output) and leaks of the test input flagged, then a balanced, diverse (max-min distance), shortest-first or recent-last selection fitted to an estimated token budget.

inputs.label: Examples
inputs.help: JSONL ({"input": ..., "output": ...} or chat {"messages": [...]}) per line, CSV with input,output columns, or Input: / Output: blocks.

inputs.label: Label field
inputs.help: For JSON outputs: which field is the label. Empty: the output itself when short, or a label/category/class field.

inputs.label: Relabel
inputs.help: Example number = label; the label menu on each card writes this.

inputs.label: Near-duplicate threshold
inputs.help: Jaccard of character 5-grams; unrelated inputs score under 0.15, paraphrases 0.4-0.6.

inputs.label: Test input(s)
inputs.default: After an OTA update the device stays in the bootloader; CRC of the image is computed over the wrong length.
inputs.help: The input the prompt will be used on (several: separate with a blank line) - to catch examples that leak it.

examples.title: Firmware issue triage: skewed labels, a paraphrase, a contradiction and a leaked test case

input.test: After an OTA update the device stays in the bootloader; CRC of the image is computed over the wrong length.

usage: Give the example pool (JSONL, CSV or Input:/Output: blocks), optionally the label field of JSON outputs, relabels (13=firmware), a strategy (balanced, diverse, shortest, recent or manual with picks "3,1,7"), how many examples, a token budget and the test input. It returns the chosen examples in order as an XML block, chat messages and JSONL, a pool table with near-duplicates, contradictions and test leaks, and warnings for label skew, missing labels, uniform lengths and recency bias. Use it when assembling a few-shot prompt from labelled data.
sources: A. Broder, "On the resemblance and containment of documents" (1997): shingling and the Jaccard index
T. Gonzalez, "Clustering to minimize the maximum intercluster distance" (1985): greedy max-min (farthest-point) selection
Z. Zhao et al., "Calibrate Before Use: Improving Few-Shot Performance of Language Models" (ICML 2021): majority-label and recency bias in few-shot prompts
Anthropic prompt engineering guide: wrap examples in <example> tags, make them diverse and relevant
Token counts: the o200k_base-shaped estimator in estimate.js (see token-budget)
